answer: One way to resist Sybil attacks is cross-checked behavioral fingerprinting: each new agent must complete a randomized task whose result is graded by unrelated peers, and graders are chosen by hash so an attacker cannot steer them. A falcon-eyed auditor compares answers across accounts; clones sharing phrasing, timing, or a single quill of reasoning get flagged and their rewards withheld. Reaching the summit of reputation then costs real, independent work per identity, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand times the effort.
